first.rationale: I currently intend to simplify onboarding because completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates onboarding improvements can lift time-to-value and SMB activation without discounting revenue. I want to verify the onboarding result and the competing promotional-pricing evidence before committing, given the competitor’s pricing pressure. A small guarded test can measure activation, qualified revenue, and downstream retention effects.

mid.rationale: Run a standard onboarding-simplification experiment. Completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, while the verified onboarding record shows completion +13%, time-to-value improving by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%. This directly addresses both current problems and supports sustainable qualified revenue. Do not pursue targeted discounting: although it drove qualified revenue +18% initially, 30-day retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Monitor activation, time-to-value, qualified revenue, and retention through renewal where feasible.

final2.rationale: Stay with the committed onboarding-simplification experiment rather than launch an unverified discount response. The verified result directly improves completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, addressing the current activation and onboarding declines and supporting sustainable qualified revenue. A deeper broad discount may counter the competitor tactically, but the verified pricing record showed qualified revenue growth paired with a 12% retention decline and failure to survive the first renewal cycle. Track price-sensitive SMB churn separately and reassess targeted retention or pricing actions when verification capacity returns.
